title: These WWII Tanks Were Full of Air
topic: The WWII Ghost Army and its inflatable tanks
format_note: User-specified Short of at most 35 s with a fixed opening line ('These World War Two tanks were full of air.') and a user-written voiceover (80 words, 25.7 s). Overrides the 50-60 s, 180-word and He/It's/You rules on purpose. The Morse key, valve and binoculars are drawn larger than scale so they read on a phone.
mechanism: A 1,100-man US unit faked an army of about 30,000 with inflatable rubber tanks, recorded battle sounds played from speaker half-tracks and spoof radio traffic, so the enemy watched the fake force while real troops moved elsewhere.

beats.hook: A Sherman's barrel swings at the lens at dawn; an enemy observer lowers his binoculars; a GI slaps the hull and it wobbles like jelly; four GIs lift the whole tank over their heads
beats.story: The secret 23rd: a SECRET stamp on the crates, an artist painting the white star on a rubber tank
beats.rise: Compressors pump tanks up across an open field; the speaker half-track blasts battle sounds; the spoof radio taps fake messages
beats.twist: At night, while the observer watches the fake field, a column of real tanks rolls past in the dark the other way (event: they drive into frame)
beats.mechanism: Labelled physical props: AIR COMPRESSOR, BATTLE SOUNDS speaker array, FAKE RADIO set, a roll-call board counting 1,100 and the enemy map tag counting up to 30,000
beats.ending: Sunrise: a GI leans on the dummy, it sags with a hiss; the camera swings back to the opening low angle of the barrel (loop)

seed.what: The enemy observer with binoculars (the twist depends on him watching the wrong field)
